title: Marie de Médicis (Brulart) to Savary de Brèves, Rome, 15 Sept and 10 Nov 1610 (BnF fr. 3789)

documents.shelfmark: BnF fr. 3789, stamped f. 19r (notice no. 12, 'fol. 21'); DECODE R2076

transcription.notes: Corrected 20 Oct 2026 against the key (alignment.tsv): 72 and 79 are overbarred; '3ᵈ' is two signs. The 21 Sept count (40, ct_nov.txt) split 'a ,' style comma codes.

documents.shelfmark: BnF fr. 3789, stamped f. 17r (notice no. 11); DECODE R2075

transcription.notes: Two passages in one letter. Corrected 20 Oct 2026 (alignment.tsv): 72 overbarred; 't u' is one glyph (tu = U). The 21 Sept count was 60 (ct_sept.txt).

documents.shelfmark: unknown (two crops, b1 and b2, supplied by George Lasry with his 2022 CTTS project; possibly Henri IV to Brèves, R2077, BnF fr. 3541 ff. 4-7, not established)

system.summary: Henri IV-Brèves cipher of 1610 (key BnF fr. 3462, Gallica view 112): homophonic alphabet of 2-5 signs per letter, comma-marked letter codes for common words, plain and overbarred number codes.
system.sibling_key: BnF fr. 3462 view 112, the key of Henri IV to Brèves 5 Jan 1610 (DECODE R2077; R2077's note mistypes the shelfmark as 3642)
system.notes: Key fits 95 of 98 glyphs (86 directly on view 112, 3 probable entries, 6 barred numbers off the page as corroborated by Tomokiyo); 3 signs conflict, so Marie's table may differ in a few cells.

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo (louisxiii.htm) and DECODE R2075/R2076: 'not deciphered'. Henri IV's own letter (R2077) was broken by Lasry, Biermann and Tomokiyo in 2021; its decryption is not on DECODE.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: beam.py (beam search over key-derived candidate letters, fr-1600-letters LM; 21 Sept, failed)

solution.what: Located no. 12 in the scan: notice folios run two ahead of the stamped foliation; letter is stamped f. 19 (canvas 36).
Transcribed the 10 Nov passage and the 15 Sept sibling from full-resolution canvases.
Applied values from the interlinear-deciphered Villeroy 1605 letter in the same volume (f. 26).
Tomokiyo louisxiii.htm and DECODE: R2077 broken by Lasry/Biermann/Tomokiyo 2021; key in BnF fr. 3642, photo on R2077.
Read the 833-px key photo: alphabet, t-z box, codes 4-99, comma letter codes, barred 4-46; M-Z codes missing.
Beam search over each sign's candidate letters from the key reading, scored with fr-1600-letters.
Found Brèves's reply of 9 Dec 1610 to the 10 Nov letter (Cinq cents de Colbert 351, pp. 724-730); it paraphrases the Savoy/Spain points, no quotation of the ciphered words.

Brice Dudout (with Claude and Codex) located the key at BnF fr. 3462, Gallica btv1b9058227h view 112, and deciphered both passages with it by a manual glyph-by-glyph alignment (emails 16 and 19 Oct 2026).
Satoshi Tomokiyo confirmed to Brice that R2077's '3642' is a mistyping of fr. 3462 and corroborated barred 72 que, 79 re, 86 se, 90 tion (41 = leur).
Gallica IIIF returned 403 (Cloudflare); used the key image (1800 x 1580 px) and line crops from Brice's CC BY 4.0 repository.
Re-read our 21 Sept transcription against the key: bars on 72/79, 3ᵈ split, 'tu' one glyph; several of our letters lumped distinct key shapes.

Compared each of the 98 glyphs with the cell of view 112 it matches (alignment.tsv): 86 key, 3 probable, 6 off page (Tomokiyo), 3 conflict (re[c]ognoissant has b, one s without an S cell, acompagne[z] = E3 or Z2).
Settled three of Brice's brackets (am[b]ition, foi[b]lesse, [s]entant); proposed 'acompagnee' (E3) agreeing with 'ambition'.

George Lasry (PR #61): his 2022 CTTS project for the Henri IV-Brèves key, improved with Opus 5.5 in Oct 2026: full CTTS key (letters, comma-letter words, barred numbers, repeat sign s-), a second document in the key (two crops, 766 cipher elements, 763 valued) with French reading and English translation, and his decryption of the 10 Nov 1610 passage, agreeing with Dudout's reading.

Review on merging PR #61: verify.py passes (hashes, deterministic token alignment, links); the second s of recognoissant is Lasry's repeat sign s-, used ten times in the longer document, which closes one conflict (96/98 Marie glyphs supported); re[c]ognoissant stays a B1/C conflict; the table's M column has a/b/c/d-shaped signs while Lasry's CTTS labels a=M, b=C, c=S, d=P are glyph names, not facsimiles; 'm, = dict' checked on the assembled key image ('Dict - m,'), not a typo. BMPs dropped, PNGs recompressed losslessly, assembled key halved with assemble_key.py to rebuild it.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): Dudout's reading (reading.txt) on the project's transcriptions ct_sept_v2/ct_nov_v2; George Lasry's CTTS transcriptions, decryptions and edited texts (lasry2022/ctts/) for 10 Nov and the additional document b1/b2 as separate entries; the Codex edition reading_fr.txt with translation_en.txt as a separate entry; key_file Lasry's CTTS key.

v3 verification: 15sept1610 and 10nov1610 were scored on the two-passage reading.txt (0.0) and Lasry's 3_edits.txt (0.5, line labels and ellipses). Each passage written out as its whole sentence (15sept1610_reading.md, 10nov1610_reading.md, 10nov1610_lasry_reading.md): explicit-hole 0.75, 1.0, 1.0. All three keep read.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: Brice Dudout found that the Henri IV-Brèves key of 1610 (BnF fr. 3462 view 112, filed for another letter) fits Marie's passages and deciphered them; the project's sign-by-sign check finds 95 of 98 glyphs supported.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Marie passages: alignment.tsv, 98 glyphs: 86 key + 3 probable + 6 Tomokiyo-corroborated + 1 repeat sign (Lasry, PR #61) = 96; 2 conflicts counted as unread. Additional document: lasry2022/verification.json, 766 cipher elements, 3 unresolved. 859/864.

gaps.detail: B1 (b) on view 112; the word needs c. Lasry's CTTS key (PR #61) gives the sign C from this word only; his longer document does not use it.
E3 (e, 'acompagnee') or Z2 (z); the cells differ by a stroke.
N-Z page of the key not in hand; values corroborated by Tomokiyo and independently in Lasry's CTTS key (PR #61), counted as read.

gaps.item: additional document (Lasry, PR #61): barred 74 and 75 (3 tokens), shelfmark and date
gaps.detail: the N-Z page of the key is not in hand; the crops carry no heading, date or signature

texts.label: 15 Sept 1610, f. 17r (R2075), Brice Dudout's reading
texts.summary: Marie de Médicis to Brèves, two ciphered passages on Savoy's son's journey to Spain: their persistence in raising difficulties "will show too plainly their malice and ambition", which she judges would be "accompanied by imprudence and weakness" given the present state of their affairs. Deciphered by Brice Dudout with the Henri IV-Brèves key (BnF fr. 3462 view 112) and checked sign by sign here (alignment.tsv).

reading_review.note: v3 verification 23 Oct 2026: the sweep scored reading.txt as a whole (both passages, clear text in braces, comment lines; 0.0 on 32 words), a false alarm. The 15 Sept sentence written out whole in 15sept1610_reading.md (clear words of the letter around the cipher, Brice Dudout's brackets kept as holes): 0.75 explicit-hole and plain (3/4 sentences, hole rate 0.045). Rests on Dudout's decipherment checked sign by sign (alignment.tsv).

texts.label: 10 Nov 1610, f. 19r (R2076), Brice Dudout's reading
texts.summary: In mid-sentence, on Savoy's disarmament after Henri IV's death and Spain's refusal: "the pope, recognising their arrogance and sensing his own timidity", would not press Spain to the point of disarmament only to receive the shame of a flat refusal. Brice Dudout's reading, checked sign by sign here (alignment.tsv).

reading_review.note: v3 verification 23 Oct 2026: scored on the two-passage reading.txt (0.0), a false alarm. The 10 Nov sentence written out whole in 10nov1610_reading.md: 1.0 explicit-hole (3/3, hole rate 0.062), plain 0.333 (1610 unaccented spellings arogance, timidite). Rests on Dudout's decipherment checked sign by sign; Lasry's CTTS decipherment agrees.

texts.label: 10 Nov 1610, image 3, George Lasry's CTTS transcription and decryption
texts.summary: George Lasry's CTTS decipherment of the same passage (2022, improved with Opus 5.5 in Oct 2026, PR #61): mechanical CTTS decryption and his edited text. It agrees with Dudout's reading word for word and shows the second s of recognoissant as the key's repeat sign.

reading_review.note: v3 verification 23 Oct 2026: 3_edits.txt scored 0.5 because of Lasry's line labels and the two '…' marking that the excerpt starts and ends inside the letter. Joined into running text in 10nov1610_lasry_reading.md: 1.0 explicit-hole and plain (23 words). Agrees with Dudout's reading (Sa Sainteté = nomenclator 4, le pape).

texts.label: Additional document, image b1 (George Lasry's CTTS files)
texts.summary: A letter in the same key, read by George Lasry (CTTS, 2022; improved with Opus 5.5, Oct 2026): marriage negotiations under aliases (La Hale, Le Cormier, La Cheville, Pindare, Saint Paul). Shelfmark and date not established; it may be Henri IV to Brèves (R2077), but Lasry asks that it not be identified with R2077 without a matching archival image.

texts.label: Additional document, image b2 (George Lasry's CTTS files)
texts.summary: Second image of the same document (Lasry's CTTS files): the reaction to an alliance, calm at home and friendship with neighbours, "au grand desplaisir de Sa Sainteté"; barred 74 and 75 unresolved.

texts.label: Additional document and 10 Nov excerpt, edited reading with Codex's image checks (PR #61)
texts.summary: The edition prepared by Codex in the contribution, taking Lasry's CTTS key and reading as its base and departing from his edited export where the images support it (Pindare not Vendosme?, prester l'oreille not rejetter?, desquels not de Lesdiguières?, rompu omitted). Lasry's own edited text is in ctts/edited/, unchanged, for comparison.
